newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle futures end higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle futures end higher.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed higher with buying motivated by gains in hog and pork belly futures, traders said.
USDA last week reported there will be fewer hogs later this year than analysts expected, which may mean less meat and possibly higher hog and cattle prices then, traders said.

Cash cattle markets were quiet Monday, prompting CME traders to say buying in cattle futures appeared to be in reaction to higher CME hog futures. Cash feedlot sources said $66.00 per cwt bids were passed at Plains-area feedlots Monday and cattle generally were priced at $68.00.
"This thing is grain- and hogs-driven right now. There is not much in the cash (markets)," a CME trader said of the cash cattle market.
Feeder cattle drew strength from higher deferred live cattle futures and lower deferred CBOT corn futures, traders said.

USDA on Monday estimated 81.416 million U.S. acres will be planted to corn this year and 68.80 million acres to soybeans, both of which exceeded the average of analysts' estimates. As a result, feeder cattle traders assumed there will be ample supplies of lower-priced grain next fall for feeding, which should enhance demand for feeder cattle.
Live cattle closed up 0.900 to 0.050 cent per lb with April up 0.475 at 68.425 cents. Feeder cattle closed up 1.175 to 0.525 cent with April up 0.825 at 69.375 cents.
